as_told.title: NASA transient lunar phenomena archive centred on Aristarchus

plain: The claim is that the Moon is not as dead as it looks. Over the centuries, watchers have reported short-lived lights and changes on its surface, known as lunar transient phenomena. The researcher Randall Carlson tells Michels, without naming a source, that there are "hundreds of examples of the moon outgassing carbon dioxide, outgassing water vapor, things like that." A second guest, the researcher Maaneli Derakhshani, puts it differently on another episode. He says "NASA has this archive of transient lunar phenomena dating back hundreds of years" from amateur and professional astronomers. In his telling the reports cluster around a crater called Aristarchus. Neither guest names a further source for what they summarise. If the reports hold up, something keeps happening on the Moon, whether natural venting or something stranger.
